questions.question: Three articles are bought at Rs. 180 each. One of them is sold at a loss of 10%, If the other two articles are sold so as to gain 20% on the whole transaction, then what is the gain percentage on the two articles?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost of three articles = Rs. 180 each

One article sold at loss = 10%

Two articles sold at gain = 20%

**Formula used:**

Gain% = Gain/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

Cost of three articles = Rs. (180 × 3)

⇒ Rs. 540

Total gain percentage on whole transaction = 20%

Then,

SP of all three articles = (540 × 120/100)

⇒ 648

SP of first article = (180 – 180 × 10%)

⇒ (180 –18)

⇒ 162

CP of other two article = 360

SP of other two article = (648 – 162)

⇒ 486

Gain on two article = (486 – 360)

⇒ 126

Gain% = (126/360 × 100)

⇒ 35%

**∴ The gain percentage on two articles is 35%**

questions.question: A man sold his cycle at 17% loss. If he had sold it for Rs. 1,056 more, he would have made 5% profit, The cost price of the cycle is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total percentage gap = Loss% + Profit% (since signs are opposite).

Gap = 17% + 5% = 22%.

Given that 22% of CP = ₹1,056.

Cost Price (100%) = (1,056 ÷ 22) × 100.

CP = 48 × 100 = ₹4,800.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss percentage = 17%

Profit percentage = 5%

Difference in Selling Price = ₹1,056

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 − Loss)%

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit)%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4586f5125a1a726f64eb75c23f8aa0cb873f018b636498179afcbcafedae6424.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the cycle be ₹x.

⇒ First Selling Price (SP₁) = x × (100 − 17)/100 = 0.83x

⇒ Second Selling Price (SP₂) = x × (100 + 5)/100 = 1.05x

⇒ According to the question: SP₂ − SP₁ = 1,056

⇒ 1.05x − 0.83x = 1,056

⇒ 0.22x = 1,056

⇒ x = 1,056 ÷ 0.22

⇒ x = 1,05,600 ÷ 22

⇒ x = 4,800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Difference Rule

When moving from a loss to a profit, the effective percentage change is the sum of the loss and profit percentages: CP = (Price Difference) ÷ (Profit% + Loss%) × 100.

Basic Profit and Loss Relation

Profit = SP − CP and Loss = CP − SP. Both percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise.

Successive Percentage Change

If an item is sold through multiple hands, the final price is CP × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100) where r represents the profit/loss rate at each stage.

questions.question: A man earns a profit of 45 percent by selling a bike for a certain price. If he sells that bike at double the price, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the bike be 100 units.

Selling Price (SP) at 45% profit = 100 + 45 = 145 units.

New SP when sold at double the price = 2 × 145 = 290 units.

New Profit = New SP − CP = 290 − 100 = 190 units.

Since the base CP is 100 units, the profit percentage is directly the profit amount.

**∴ The correct answer is 190%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial profit percentage = 45%

New Selling Price = 2 × Initial Selling Price

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90b9a6846371864149e30d5fa1d627c2df919edb190e25b3ee31a3d6ae01c63a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the bike be x.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP) = x × (100 + 45) ÷ 100 = 1.45x

⇒ New Selling Price = 2 × Initial SP = 2 × 1.45x = 2.90x

⇒ New Profit = New Selling Price − CP

⇒ New Profit = 2.90x − x = 1.90x

⇒ New Profit % = (New Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ New Profit % = (1.90x ÷ x) × 100 = 190%

**∴ The correct answer is 190%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

MP is the price printed on the article. Discount is always calculated on the MP. Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Profit

When an article is sold sequentially by multiple sellers, the effective SP is calculated cumulatively: Final SP = CP × (100 + P₁%) ÷ 100 × (100 + P₂%) ÷ 100.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer professes to sell goods at CP but uses a false weight, the profit percentage is calculated as: Profit % = (Error ÷ (True Value − Error)) × 100.

questions.question: A man buys a watch for ₹250 and sells it for ₹300. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price = Rs250

Selling price = Rs300

**Formula Used:**

Profit = S.P. -C.P. 

Profit% = (Profit/C.P.) × 100 

Where, S.P.= Selling price, C.P.= Cost price 

**Calculation:**

Here, C.P. = Rs250, S.P. =Rs300

⇒ Profit = S.P. - C.P. = (300 -250) = Rs50

⇒ Profit% = (Profit/C.P.) × 100 = (50/250) × 100 = 20%

**Hence, the required profit percentage is 20%.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper makes a 15% profit on a sale. He would have made 18%, if he had sold it for Rs.18 more. The cost price of the article is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A shopkeeper makes a 15% profit on a sale. He would have made 18%, if he had sold it for Rs.18 more.

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) + Profit

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be Rs. x

Selling Price at 15% profit = x + 0.15x = 1.15x

Selling Price at 18% profit = x + 0.18x = 1.18x

Given, 1.18x = 1.15x + 18

⇒ 1.18x - 1.15x = 18

⇒ 0.03x = 18

⇒ x = dfrac{18}{0.03}

⇒ x = 600

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price is Rs. 143. If profit percentage is 26 percent, then what is the selling price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between the Selling Price and Cost Price is the Profit.

Profit = 26% of Cost Price ⇒ 26 units = Rs. 143

Selling Price = 100% (CP) + 26% (Profit) = 126 units

Selling Price = (143 ÷ 26) × 126 = 11 × 63 = 693

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 693.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between Cost Price (CP) and Selling Price (SP) = Profit = Rs. 143

Profit percentage = 26%

 Cost Price (100%) Profit (26%) Rs. 143

• Selling Price (126%) = Rs. 693 Profit and Loss Visualisation 

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP

SP = CP + Profit

**Calculations:**

⇒ 143 = (26 ÷ 100) × CP

⇒ CP = (143 × 100) ÷ 26

⇒ CP = 11 × 50

⇒ CP = Rs. 550

⇒ SP = CP + Profit

⇒ SP = 550 + 143

⇒ SP = Rs. 693

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 693.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). Thus, Profit = SP − CP. Conversely, a loss happens when CP is greater than SP.

Profit Percentage Base

Profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless the question specifically mentions calculating it on the Selling Price. Formula: Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Direct Selling Price Formula

When the cost price and profit percentage are known, the selling price can be directly calculated using the multiplier formula: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: Arvind bought eight washing machines at Rs. 16,000 each and sold all of them at a total price of Rs. 1,12,640. Find his profit or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

CP of eight washing machines = Rs. 16,000 each

SP of eight washing machine = Rs. 1,12,640

**Formula used:**

Loss = CP – SP

Loss% = Loss/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

CP of eight washing machines = Rs. (16,000 × 8)

⇒ 128,000

SP of eight washing machine = Rs. 1,12,640

Loss = CP – SP

⇒ Rs. (128,000 – 112,640)

⇒ Rs. 15,360

Loss% = Loss/CP × 100

⇒ (15,360/128,000 × 100)

⇒ (15,360/1280)

⇒ 12%

**∴ The required loss% is 12%**
